purpose: Bazel 9.3's worker spawn strategy (WorkerSpawnRunner, WorkerParser, WorkerPoolImpl, SingleplexWorker, JSON/proto WorkerProtocol): the default strategy list [worker, sandboxed, local], supports-workers / supports-multiplex-workers ('1' only), requires-worker-protocol (json, proto, invalid), worker-key-mnemonic, --worker_max_instances, --worker_max_multiplex_instances, --noworker_multiplex, --worker_sandboxing, --worker_extra_flag, --experimental_worker_strict_flagfiles, --experimental_worker_allowlist, --worker_verbose, --spawn_strategy/--strategy interplay, the worker argv (flag files removed, --persistent_worker appended, argv[0] absolute), its environment, each WorkRequest (arguments from the expanded @flagfile, the inputs list with hex-text digests, request ids, verbosity, Gson HTML-safe JSON escaping), tree-artifact inputs expanded, and the failure messages (non-zero exit code, crash without response, unparseable response, missing flagfile, invalid protocol). The fixture worker (pkg/worker.py) appends its process starts and requests to <trace>/trace.jsonl; pids are replaced by ordinals.
